title: Warcraft Was Almost a Warhammer Game
hook: In 1993 Blizzard's co-founder wanted to license Warhammer for the studio's first strategy game, and the deal went nowhere. Would you have played World of Warhammer?
script: Did you know the first Warcraft game was almost a licensed Warhammer game? Back in 1993, Blizzard was a tiny studio that had been building licensed comic book games for DC Comics. The team was hooked on Dune Two and wanted to make its own real time strategy game. Blizzard co-founder Allen Adham hoped to license the Warhammer universe so the game would sell on a name people already knew. Lead programmer Patrick Wyatt later wrote that the idea never gained traction on business terms. The developers also wanted to control their own universe after their rough experience with the comic book games. So the deal died, and Blizzard built its own world instead. Warhammer still left a mark, though. Wyatt has said it was a huge inspiration for Warcraft's art style. Years after launch, his own father handed him a box of Warhammer miniatures and said they looked like his game. Warcraft: Orcs and Humans shipped in November 1994. The world it created went on to power World of Warcraft, which launched a decade later in 2004. Imagine logging into World of Warhammer every night instead. Would you have played it? Follow for more gaming history.
